meta.title: feat: integrate x86-64 TCO with c-unwind ABI for instruction execution
meta.body_summary: Add x86-64 Tail Call Optimization in instruction execution loop via assembly stubs with c-unwind ABI to eliminate stack frame overhead while preserving panic unwinding, claiming >50% performance improvement.

perf_labels.notes: Devin added x86-64 TCO assembly stubs; CI benchmarks showed up to 50% slowdown, contradicting performance claim; PR auto-closed after 7 days without maintainer review.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 165 changed lines, this is a small edit by absolute volume, concentrated in a new tco.rs module and minor interpreter changes. As a low-level performance optimization PR, it was closed—not merged—because CI benchmarks consistently showed significant runtime degradation (up to 50.42% slowdown) and no human maintainer reviewed or approved the change.

review_details.concern_detail: Automated CI from github-actions and CodSpeed reported execution time regressions across multiple benchmarks (bubblesort: +50.42%, quicksort: +42.58%, etc.), contradicting the claimed >50% improvement. No human maintainer provided additional review.
review_details.performance_claim: Tail call optimization would eliminate stack frame overhead in instruction execution loop, potentially providing >50% performance improvement.
review_details.rejection_signals: PR auto-closed after 7 days of inactivity; CI benchmarks consistently showed performance degradation, no maintainer engagement.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Low-level assembly optimization with unsafe code requires verified performance gains; CI benchmarks contradicted the performance hypothesis, and the agent did not produce the expected improvement.

detection_detail.ci_auto: CodSpeed and github-actions benchmark jobs automatically compared execution times against baseline and posted regression reports.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: Multiple CI runs produced consistent regression results (e.g., bubblesort 50.42% slower), providing clear evidence against the performance improvement claim.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: PR closed automatically by Devin bot after 7 days without further commits to address regression; no human maintainer action was taken.

core_change_summary.description: Add a new tco.rs module with x86-64 assembly stubs using c‑unwind ABI for tail call optimization in the instruction execution loop; conditionally call tco_execute_one_instruction via unsafe pointer wrappers in interpreter.rs when target_arch = x86_64; include .cfi directives for unwinding.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: mod.rs only adds pub mod tco; interpreter changes are minimal (3 lines of conditional logic).
change_trajectory: Initial commit adds tco.rs (78 lines) and integrates conditional TCO calls in interpreter.rs.
Subsequent commits fix clippy lint by adding safety documentation, then use allow attribute, and finally apply nightly rustfmt formatting.
CI benchmark results are posted automatically, showing performance regressions; no substantive changes to address regression before auto-close.

review_signals.summary: Devin bot announced automatic comment/CI assistance for write-access users.
Benchmark results on commit 0a33457 show mixed but mostly regressions (verify_fibair +2.6%, regex +1.6%, etc.); later runs confirm similar patterns.
Merging will degrade performances by 50.42% overall; 11 out of 24 benchmarks regress (e.g., bubblesort +50.42%, quicksort +42.58%).
Closing due to inactivity for more than 7 days.

collaboration_trajectory: Devin opened PR with TCO integration.
CI benchmarks and CodSpeed posted performance regression data within minutes.
Agent made minor CI lint/formatter fixes but did not address performance regression.
After 7 days of inactivity, Devin bot auto‑closed the PR.
